text:
marie: Hey all — running into a weird combo of issues when consuming the JS SDK from a pnpm monorepo + edge runtime. Node resolution works locally, but when deployed to the edge (Cloudflare Workers / V8), the runtime can't load the package and TS types are wrong.

ben: ugh that sounds like the classic exports/hoisting visibility trick with pnpm. Can you paste your package.json for the SDK package and the consumer tsconfig/tsserver error?

marie: sure — SDK package.json excerpt:
```json
{"name":"@redwood/sdk","version":"0.1.0","main":"dist/index.cjs.js","module":"dist/index.esm.js","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"import":"./dist/index.esm.js","require":"./dist/index.cjs.js"}}
```
Consumer tsconfig is mostly default, and pnpm workspace layout: top-level pnpm-workspace.yaml with packages: ['packages/*']
TS error in editor: "Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk'" but `npm pack` and direct install works. Edge runtime logs: `Error: cannot find module '@redwood/sdk'` at runtime when bundling via our edge bundler.

alex: Do you have `public-hoist-pattern` or nohoist set? pnpm creates symlinks; sometimes bundlers follow hoisted layout differently. Also some bundlers don't resolve `exports` for symlinked packages.

marie: we don't use nohoist. I tried adding `node-linker=hoisted` but that broke other packages.

sam: Another culprit: some edge bundlers (esbuild config) treat symlinked workspaces as external. Check your bundler's `preserveSymlinks` / `external` settings. For Vercel/CF, bundlers will inline packages only if they are real files, not symlinks.

marie: Good call — our esbuild config had `preserveSymlinks: true` enabled. Turning it off helped find the package but then types mismatch. The editor still picks up the root's @types instead of the package's d.ts.

ben: For types, ensure your package's `types` field points to a file that actually exists in dist when used in workspace (pnpm doesn't hoist d.ts by default). Also add `exports` with `types` condition if consumers respect it: e.g.
```json
"exports": {
  "import": { "default": "./dist/index.esm.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" },
  "require": { "default": "./dist/index.cjs.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" }
}
```
(although not all resolvers use the `types` condition).

marie: tried that pattern — ESLint/TS still resolves to the workspace root. Could this be a vfs/symlink editor bug? VSCode TS server sometimes prefers workspace root `node_modules`.

alex: Yep. For a consistent DX we had to add a `typesVersions` map in package.json for the SDK consumer path. Ugly but works across editors: 
```json
"typesVersions": { "*": { "*": ["dist/*"] } }
```
That helped our monorepo at work.

marie: thanks — added typesVersions and that fixed editor errors locally. But one more thing: the edge runtime started throwing auth header errors after switching to ESM import style: `fetch` calls from our SDK didn't include Authorization in retries (it was sending twice or missing on retry). Anyone seen auth/retry interplay in edge environments?

sam: We saw that when using a wrapper around fetch which clones the Request incorrectly. Retries that recreate the Request object without `credentials: 'include'` or without copying headers will drop Authorization. If your SDK does internal retry on 5xx, ensure you clone headers explicitly: `new Request(original.url, { headers: new Headers(original.headers), method: original.method, body: original.body })`.

ben: Also check that ESM build tree-shakes away the polyfill you used earlier for node fetch — polyfills sometimes implement retries differently. In our SDK we switched to a minimal retry helper that accepts an `onRetry(request)` hook so auth headers are preserved.

marie: That explains a lot — we were using a retry wrapper from an older helper that used `request.headers.forEach` but didn't copy `Authorization` when `Headers` were a proxy in edge. Swapping to explicit copy fixed it in staging.

alex: For the workspace hoisting part, we've been gradually recommending two concrete things to teams to avoid this class of bugs:
- publish a lightweight `package.json` in packages/*/dist when local linking (postbuild cp package.json) so bundlers/readers resolve the same as published package.
- add a small `examples/workspace` in the SDK repo that shows pnpm+esbuild+vercel/CF config (including `preserveSymlinks: false` and tsserver `watchOptions` tweaks).

marie: I'm going to try the dist/package.json trick. One more ask: can we add a short doc or troubleshooting checklist to the SDK repo for monorepo consumers? Steps: pnpm workspace gotchas, exports+typesPatterns, esbuild/rollup flags, auth/retry note.

ben: +1. Please open a tiny PR in the SDK repo, add `docs/monorepo.md` and an `examples/workspace` with minimal repo. If you'd like I can pair on the example.

marie: I'll open the PR today and link it here. Thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:

dev-bot: Deploy preview for branch/monorepo-fixes available at https://deploy.preview/monorepo-fixes (auto-build includes example workspace)

ben: Awesome — linking this thread to the GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/432 — I'll add notes from our chat to the issue so we can track adding docs + tests.

marie: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/987 — includes example, dist/package.json script, and a note about retry header copying. I'll follow up if anything else pops up.

sam: If anyone runs into similar but with yarn workspaces, ping me — yarn's hoisting patterns are different and we might need separate docs.

alex: Great thread. TL;DR: symlinks + exports + types are the trifecta; add dist/package.json + typesVersions and watch your bundler `preserveSymlinks` + fix retry clone logic for auth headers.

marie: thanks all!
